# Preface {.unnumbered}

These are the lecture notes for PHIL 444, Game Theory and Social Choice, at the
University of Michigan.

The notes are based on something I wrote for an older course, so they don't cover exactly the material of what we're doing here. In particular, the last chapter is relevant to the second part of the course, but we aren't going to follow it directly.

They are the primary reading for the game theory half of the course. Giacomo
Bonanno's *Game Theory* [-@bonanno2024] is freely available online and is
worth having open alongside these notes. It covers most of the same ground in a
different voice, and it has 165 solved exercises, which these notes do not.
Where the two disagree in emphasis, follow the notes; where Bonanno goes further
than we do, that is usually deliberate.

The second half of the course works through Amartya Sen's *Collective Choice and Social Welfare* [-@sen2017] instead, so these notes stop where Sen starts. The material on
voting systems in Part II has no counterpart in Sen and is still assigned.

A PDF of the whole book is linked in the sidebar for anyone who would rather
read it in one piece.
